thought.text: The architecture is clear. Let me wait for the `pnpm install` (with `prepare` generating API clients) to finish before starting `just up`, to avoid concurrent nx runs:

reasoning_content:
OK, I understand the mechanism now:
- `attachInstance` copies nginx.conf to the proxy container and reloads it. The dev server (pnpm nx serve) gets started on the host on an allocated port, and is reachable via the proxy's host-gateway IP.

Key insight regarding `just up` in the foreground: after the container + seed completes, it runs `awaitDevServersReady` with a deadline = max(startedAt + 300 seconds, waitingSince + 120 seconds). The dev server was started before the container phase, so it's been compiling during that time. If it responds within the deadline, it's OK. If not, it's a "non-responding" warning, but the URL gets displayed, and `finishDevServers` keeps running until Ctrl-C.

Hmm — so `just up` without `--detach` is a long-running foreground command. The task says "strictly use non-interactive command options whenever possible." `just up` keeps running in the foreground indefinitely (serving the dev server). For verification, it might be better to run `just up` in the background (with setsid) and verify the endpoints via curl, and then leave it running (that's the installed state) — or run `just up --detach`? But `--detach` skips the dev server, so the citizen app/CMS/urboards (one of the 4 components in the description: "backend, CMS, citizen app, urboards") won't be served. The guide says `just serve` starts only the dev server against an already-running instance. So: run `just up --detach` (brings up backend + infrastructure + seed), then run `just serve` in the background (dev server). Both are documented options.

But wait — the cleanest "one command" is `just up`. I can run it with setsid in the background and verify. It'll keep running in the background — that's fine, it's the running state of the dev stack. The only issue: it holds the dev server's port, and `finishDevServers` will race on crash/signal. With setsid + nohup, Ctrl-C won't reach it. It'll keep running until a process exits. That's fine.

Also, pnpm's `prepare` is running now. Let's wait for it to complete.

Additionally, the dev server compiles the Angular app — on this machine (8 cores) with a warm node_modules, compilation will probably take 3–10 minutes. The readiness deadline (max of 300 seconds from start or 120 seconds of grace after container is up) might be tight, but the container is already built so `just up` should be fast.

Wait, actually — for `just up` (without --detach), the dev server starts right after pnpm install completes. pnpm's prepare (generate:api) is part of the `pnpm install` step within up.mjs. So in my background run, pnpm install is already complete (currently running prepare as a separate process 8177!). Note: `just up` runs `pnpm install` itself as a step — but my current pnpm3 run is doing the same thing. To avoid a conflict, let `just up`'s pnpm install step run — node_modules is already up to date, and prepare is already running, so the `pnpm install` step inside just up will either skip prepare (because node_modules is up to date?) or re-run it.

Hmm, pnpm runs `prepare` (the root workspace's lifecycle) on install. If node_modules is already up to date, does pnpm still run the root's prepare? pnpm v11 only re-runs lifecycle scripts when the install does something. "Already up to date" might mean prepare doesn't get re-run... Actually, in pnpm, even with "Already up to date," the root project's `prepare` script gets executed on install — in recent pnpm versions, the root's prepare runs even when there are no changes (this is how git-based installs work). But my pnpm3 is already running prepare right now. If just up's pnpm install runs in parallel, there could be a conflict (concurrent nx run-many writing to the same generated files).

Safest: wait for pnpm3 (with prepare) to finish completely, then start `just up`. The pnpm install step in just up will be fast ("Already up to date," and prepare might be skipped or rerun — but if it reruns, it's fast because the nx cache is warm).

Let's wait for pnpm3 to finish.

action.command:
for i in $(seq 1 10); do
  if ps -p 8177 > /dev/null 2>&1; then
    sleep 54;
  else
    break
  fi
done
echo "=== pnpm3 log tail ==="; tail -25 /tmp/pnpm-install3.log; echo "=== still running? ==="; ps -p 8177 -o pid,cmd 2>/dev/null || echo "pnpm3 DONE"
